text:
Alex K.: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing we split the LoadableShard surface into a pure IO Loader and a separate BackpressureCoordinator that owns warmup budgeting and scheduling. Opening discussion before PR.

Maria T.: What's the primary motivation? Cleaner tests or operational flexibility?

Alex K.: Both. We need per-model warmup policies that use signals beyond simple FIFO: request priority, tenant SLO, model variant.
Current loaders end up mixing IO and policy which makes changes risky.

Jin L.: I like the split. Rough API sketch: Loader only does reads. BackpressureCoordinator exposes RequestTokens(ctx, hint) -> (tokens, delay) + ReleaseTokens + OnEvict. Eg:

// Loader: pure reads, no scheduling
interface Loader { ReadShard(shardID string, off int64, n int) ([]byte, error) }

// Coordinator: returns token grant and optional delay hint
interface BackpressureCoordinator { RequestTokens(ctx, hint PrefetchHint) (int, time.Duration); ReleaseTokens(n int); OnEvict(shardID string) }

Samir: Clean but some tradeoffs: extra call per prefetch decision (in-process though). Also need a compat shim for legacy loaders that assume blocking semantics.

Maria T.: Semantics clarity: if coordinator returns delay > 0, loader should schedule async prefetch. If tokens==0 and delay==0 -> hard reject. Also define partial grants (tokens < requested) behavior.

Jin L.: Default coordinator can be local token-bucket: per-device burst tokens, host-global cap, tenant fairness. Dedicated deployments swap to a deterministic allocator for throughput SLAs. Separation allows A/Bing policies.

Alex K.: Telemetry: counters for prefetch_requested, prefetch_granted, prefetch_delayed_ms, evictions_during_warmup. Samir, can you add pending_prefetch_bytes gauge and prefetch_latency histogram (hot vs cold)?

Samir: Yep. Those metrics critical for tuning token sizes. Also surface tokens_used per-device.

Maria T.: Migration plan: include a default coordinator wrapper that grants immediately (no behavior change). Opt-in via model manifest flag warmup.coordinator=v2. Rollout gradually.

Jin L.: Legacy behavior: some callers rely on blocking ReadShard for side effects. Provide a BlockingReadShard adapter that requests tokens synchronously and blocks until data is read while keeping core Loader async. Document it clearly.

Alex K.: Tests: add eviction race tests (grant -> eviction before read completes) asserting OnEvict semantics and token reclamation. Also add benchmarks: baseline combined impl vs split with noop coordinator vs split with tokenized coordinator under workloads: low QPS, high QPS short seq, high QPS long seq, and bursty startup.

ops-bot: ci/build-status: flaky test_prefetch_race on linux-integration  FYI may block merge.

Samir: We'll rerun CI after PR. For perf, let's capture metrics with and without coordinator to measure overhead of extra call and gains from smarter scheduling.

Maria T.: Suggest adding fields to PrefetchHint: prefetch_priority int (higher = more urgent), is_fallback bool, model_variant string. Also include request_id for tracing.

Jin L.: Add estimated_bytes int in hint so coordinator can make better space decisions. Also add expected_ttl_ms for warmup so coordinator can avoid prefetching very short-lived prefixes.

Alex K.: Good additions. I'll incorporate those in API draft and include a compat shim + adapters. Planning to open RFC PR with API diffs, telemetry plan, migration guide, and benchmark harness. Please review once posted. :thumbsup:
